firstMismatch.cEntry: invent.c:getobj splits the requested count; wield.c:dowield finishes the split child and continues through wielding
firstMismatch.jsEntry: js/invent.js:getobj creates the split child, then js/wield.js:dowield refuses that child with UnsupportedWieldError

summary: The admitted case types #wield, selects count 2, then selects inventory item a. C invent.c:getobj reaches split_otmp and calls splitobj for the requested count. C wield.c:dowield recognizes the returned child through context.objsplit.child_oid, calls finish_splitting, and continues at the wielding label. JS invent.js:getobj already returns the split child; js/wield.js:dowield currently throws at that same child branch. The diagnosis is source-traced, but source edits are pending release of the existing wield.c:dowield reservation held by this worker’s submitted quiver delivery.

source.branch: After getobj returns an object whose id is context.objsplit.child_oid, C checks whether the currently wielded object is the split parent. If so it unsplits and follows already_wielded; otherwise it calls finish_splitting and jumps to wielding. The counted case follows the latter branch.
callers: wield.c:dowield calls invent.c:getobj with GETOBJ_PROMPT | GETOBJ_ALLOWCNT.
invent.c:getobj accepts the integer count and selected inventory key, splits the object at split_otmp, and returns the child to wield.c:dowield.
wield.c:dowield calls finish_splitting before ready_weapon through its wielding label.

evidence: The published v74 admission evaluation at source base 8f280fd706dcfdad7c302cc39301cb056753af10 records 118/168 screens, 2684/2690 RNG calls, and 118/168 cursors, with null error.
